newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM ONLINE SERVICE EYES TRADING COMMUNITY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM ONLINE SERVICE EYES TRADING COMMUNITY.

text.p: A group of Belgian publishers and technology firms is offering a new online service -- Belgium Online -- which they say is to become an important platform for secure electronic trading and a window on the country.

The service, which will be available from midnight (2200 GMT) Thursday, give users "the chance to conduct actual electronic trade," offering them access to a market with major growth potential, managing director Ludo Poelaert said.
Estimates put the volume of trade via computer-operated information networks in 1996 at $800 million, more than double the 1995 level and 40 times the 1994 rate, he told a news conference.
"(The expected 1996 volume) is still peanuts, even in relation to Belgium's gross domestic product," he added.

Belgium Online meant to prove to users that trading and conducting other financial transactions via an electronic network was safe. "Currently a lot of people are still scared to use their Visa cards on the net," he said.

Using specialised sign-on and authentication technology, financial transactions would be secure, he said, adding that Belgium Online aimed to a clearing house for such transactions and Belgium's one-stop shopping spot.
Banking services are offered by Belgian bank Credit Professionel> and the Post Office's Postcheque operation.

Belgium Online will allow companies to market themselves and look at profiles of potential counter-parties. "It will also be a referential network," Poelaert said. Advertisers will pay on a per-view basis.

Communications will be part of the package, including 'regular' e-mail and e-mail secured via encryption. Fax services are to be added from the end of October. Belgium Online's intranet will also provide access to the global Internet.
Headlines from Belgian financial daily De Financieel- Economische Tijd will be available, weather reports, newspaper clippings, medical info and cultural listings and tourist information.
Belgium Online will also offer some news from Reuters Holdings Plc , the international news and information organisation.

The service intends to offer users interactive cross-referencing so that not only information on, for instance, a cultural event is available, but users are pointed on to the ticket, hotel, restaurant and car park facilities.

Poelaerts said Belgium Online was well-placed to offer network computing services, which meant that users could download, for instance, word processing software, use it and store copy on a floppy disk.

This meant they would no longer have to own powerful computers full of software, but just needed so-called network computers. On this front Belgium Online was cooperating with Oracle Corp. of the U.S.

Poelaerts said the network in its current form could handle 10,000 users. There are 28 dial-in access points in Belgium, while the service can be connected to from 700 cities around the world at local telephone rates.
He said the shareholders had invested between 20 and 30 million Belgian francs in Belgium Online.
In its first year of operation Belgium Online expects revenue of 150 to 170 million Belgian francs. Eighty percent of the contents would be free, while 20 percent would be fee-based.
